output.summary: Deterministic verdict: FAIL (analysis-result.json#/policy_verdict). Both evaluated windows — reference (1704067200000–1704067320000) and workload-01 (1704067320000–1704067800000) — fail the latency policy: response_time_p95_ms observed 227 exceeds threshold 200 (operator lte), with matching policy_failure findings. error_count is 0 in the overall and both window summaries, and both windows have resource_verdict PASS, but the business verdict is FAIL for each window. Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core, so candidate lag values (e.g., association-04 best_lag 2000ms rho 0.588, association-08 best_lag 4000ms rho 0.657, association-09 best_lag 3000ms rho 0.584) cannot be read as temporal order; all correlation headline selections are UNAVAILABLE with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, and no p-values were produced. Anomaly checks report NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE for all four series, with 30 suppressed short episodes for the response series. Recommended next steps: verify clocks first, inspect raw latency/downstream series, and rerun with varied, stepped load before drawing any causal hypothesis. This advice is interpretive and does not change the FAIL verdict.

hypotheses.observation: Policy checks for both windows report response_time_p95_ms observed 227, operator lte, threshold 200, status FAIL; findings list a latency policy_failure for each window, and both window summaries give business_verdict FAIL with resource_verdict PASS.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The measured p95 tail latency violates the 200ms threshold in both windows; the zero error counts and PASS resource verdicts do not offset this business-level failure.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the per-interval response_time_p95_ms series and confirm the 227ms value is computed from the same samples as the policy check (window summaries report sample_count 7200 for reference and 28800 for workload-01).

hypotheses.observation: resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core; every correlation headline selection is UNAVAILABLE with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED and reasons OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED or PAIR_NOT_EVALUABLE.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Without verified clock alignment between generator, service, and telemetry sources, the best_lag_ms values reported by candidate correlation pairs cannot be interpreted as lead/lag or temporal cause of the latency failure.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization across the load generator, service, and telemetry sources before assigning any temporal meaning to reported lag values.

hypotheses.observation: generator request_starts and target_rate are constant at 60 req/s (min, mean, max all 60) in both the reference and workload-01 windows, and response p95=227 and p99=248 are identical in the two window summaries.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The run sustained a flat load of 60 req/s and the tail latency metrics are identical in both windows, so the latency failure cannot be attributed to a load step between windows based on this evidence.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Compare against a prior baseline run and examine the time series of response_time_p95_ms rather than relying only on window aggregates.

hypotheses.observation: association-04 (cpu-queue) reports status CANDIDATE best_lag 2000ms best_lag_rho 0.588; association-08 (downstream-wait) reports CANDIDATE best_lag 4000ms best_lag_rho 0.657; association-09 (generator-threads) reports CANDIDATE best_lag 3000ms best_lag_rho 0.584; association-01 and association-02 are BELOW_EFFECT; all report controls_used [] and include reason CONSTANT_CONTROL.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: These stored rank correlations suggest candidate associations between resource series and response_time_p95_ms, but they remain hypotheses: requested control target-request-rate was dropped (CONSTANT_CONTROL), no p-values are available, and clock alignment is unverified.
hypotheses.recommended_check: After clock verification, inspect the raw cpu-queue, downstream-wait, and generator-threads series against response_time_p95_ms and run a load-varying experiment to test each candidate association.

hypotheses.observation: anomaly check workload-01-response reports NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE with reference_median 227, reference_mad 0, reason ZERO_MAD, and suppressed_short_episodes 30; the diagnostic summary reports episodes_reported 0, anomalies_tested 4, pairs_evaluable 5, pairs_tested 8, status COMPLETE.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The response series is flat around 227ms with zero MAD in the reference window, so the anomaly check found no material change; the 30 suppressed short episodes are not reported as material.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Examine the raw response-time series and the suppressed short episodes to see whether brief p95 deviations recur and whether they align with any candidate association (after clock verification).

hypotheses.observation: resource policy checks for system-cpu-work and system-db-work are PASS in both windows; cpu_work has mean 0.15 and max 0.16, db_work has mean 0.015, and both window summaries give resource_verdict PASS.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The resource rules evaluated as PASS while the latency rule fails; this does not prove spare capacity and does not rule out a resource-related contributor to the 227ms p95.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Collect additional telemetry not covered here (runtime heap, GC, network, and downstream dependency stats) and inspect them for contributors to the observed tail latency.

recommendations.action: Verify clock synchronization across the load generator, service, and telemetry sources before interpreting any best_lag_ms values.
recommendations.rationale: resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, so the candidate lags (1000–4000ms) have no temporal meaning without verified clocks.

recommendations.action: Inspect the per-interval response_time_p95_ms series and review the 30 suppressed short episodes for the response anomaly check.
recommendations.rationale: p95=227 exceeds the 200ms threshold in both windows; knowing whether the exceedance is sustained or episodic guides the next experiment.

recommendations.action: Rerun the test with multiple stepped target rates while keeping other conditions identical, after verifying clocks.
recommendations.rationale: The run kept target_rate and request_starts constant at 60 req/s in both windows, so the relationship between load and tail latency cannot be established from this run.

recommendations.action: Collect per-transaction latency and downstream dependency traces to test the downstream-wait candidate association.
recommendations.rationale: association-08 reports status CANDIDATE (best_lag 4000ms, best_lag_rho 0.657) but with CONSTANT_CONTROL, no p-value, and unverified clocks, so it remains an untested hypothesis.

recommendations.action: Review the latency policy threshold (200ms on p95) and confirm it matches the intended SLO; if intended, retain it and treat the run as a genuine FAIL.
recommendations.rationale: The product verdict is FAIL because observed 227 exceeds 200 in both windows; this is a policy configuration decision available to the operator and does not change the recorded verdict.

recommendations.action: After clock verification, rerun or extend the test so that the correlation analysis can produce headline selections instead of UNAVAILABLE.
recommendations.rationale: All headline selections were UNAVAILABLE (OBSERVATION_COUNT_UNSUPPORTED or PAIR_NOT_EVALUABLE) with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, so no statistically supported association can be reported from this run.

caveats: Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core; any best_lag_ms values (e.g., 1000–4000ms) must not be read as lead/lag or causal ordering until clocks are verified.
Correlation uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED and all headline selections are UNAVAILABLE; BELOW_EFFECT, CANDIDATE, and INSUFFICIENT_DATA are product states, not proof of cause or of absence of cause.

Counts appear at different scopes and are not directly comparable: overall sample_count 36000, reference window 7200, workload-01 window 28800; throughput denominators also differ (600033, 120000, 480000), and these are not inconsistent because they measure different scopes.
error_count 0 and resource_verdict PASS do not prove absence of a problem or spare capacity, and they do not offset the FAIL business verdict.
Anomaly checks returned NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE partly due to ZERO_MAD and suppressed 30 short episodes; a flat series does not prove stable response behavior, and only 4 anomalies were tested.
The reference window already recorded p95=227, so the workload-01 window did not introduce the FAIL; this run alone cannot identify the cause of the tail latency.
The verdict remains FAIL regardless of advisory recommendations; this output is an interpretation only and does not modify the recorded verdict.
